Subject: Candidate feedback alignment — Priya Shah / offer timing

Team — quick escalation. We just wrapped the panel for Priya (SWE, platform). Monica has the logistics, but there's a pretty wide spread on scores: two interviewers gave 4s, one gave a 2, one gave a 5. Marcus flagged leadership-impact examples that argue for L5; others called out unknowns around system design depth.

I want to move fast on timing (candidate has a competing verbal), but I don't want to skip calibration. Can HR weigh in on two things:
- Process: if we have split feedback, what standards do we use to confirm leveling before sending an offer?
- Interim option: if we can't reach consensus today, is manager discretion + sign-on acceptable to move quickly?

Monica — attaching the candidate resume and the scorecard export so you have everything. Marcus — can you summarize the key evidence that supports a higher band (2–3 bullets)? I can escalate to Lauren if needed but want to avoid pinging VPs unless necessary.

Thanks,
Dylan

--

Quick summary from my side:
- Candidate timeline: Priya received a verbal from another company yesterday and expects a formal offer by EOW. She prefers Redwood but needs a decision window of ~48 hours.
- Compensation constraints: recruiting sees L4 base slot available on the hiring team budget; L5 would require comp-band exception or reallocation.
- Panel notes: technical depth good for API design and caching; one interviewer had concerns on large-scale tradeoffs (scalability for 10k qps) — those concerns drove the 2 score. Others cited strong cross-team leadership examples.

Happy to coordinate a short calibration call. If we proceed with a verbal offer, I can present two options to the candidate: L4 base (standard) + discretionary sign-on vs. hold for calibration and aim for L5 (longer timeline).

Dylan / team — quick set of bullets from my interview and perspective:
- Ownership & impact: Priya described leading a cross-functional migration that reduced latency by ~40% on a production caching layer; she owned design tradeoffs, rollout plan, and post-mortem. That's L5 behavioral evidence.
- System design: solid architecture choices, but didn't fully address extreme-scale failure modes (the 2 score interview). My read is that the gap is addressable and we can mitigate with a short onboarding plan.
- Leadership: demonstrated mentoring and cross-team coordination on multiple projects.

If we care primarily about near-term execution on the platform team, I believe she is L5-ready and worth offering at L5. If comp constraints block that, manager discretion to offer L4 + $15k sign-on and a 6-month review to bump to L5 would be acceptable. Happy to take 15 minutes to calibrate with Neha.

-Marcus
Staff Engineer (interview panel lead)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Candidate feedback alignment — Priya Shah / offer timing

Thanks for the context. Process notes / recommendation: 
1) Calibration: for split panels we run a short readout with a calibrated interviewer (usually a senior hiring manager or TP) and HR. That conversation (15–20m) looks at evidence against the rubric and attempts to reconcile differences. I can join today at 11:30 or tomorrow morning.
2) If time is tight: manager discretion is supported for competitive timelines, with two controls — (a) an explicit manager-led development plan to close identified gaps, (b) a documented sign-on / performance review checkpoint (typically 6 months) tied to leveling. We can include a conditional comp uplift in the offer letter to be executed upon successful review.
3) Paperwork: if you proceed with manager discretion, please attach the panel notes and the compensatory rationale to the offer packet; HR will sign off on the discretionary sign-on amount up to $20k without exec approval. Anything higher requires VP approval.

Recommendation: hold a 15m calibration now (I can make 11:30 today), and if Marcus & Dylan remain aligned on L5, raise to Lauren only if the sign-on needs exceed $20k. If we still need to move faster than the calibration slot allows, approve manager discretion (L4 + $15k) and Monica can issue a verbal in the next 24 hours.

Attachments: comp-band-reference_Q1_2026.pdf

-Neha
Talent Partner, People & Talent
Redwood Inference

- Offer approach: verbal offer today for L4 base + $15,000 sign-on (manager discretion).
- Documentation: Monica to attach the panel export, Marcus's bulleted evidence, and the onboarding development plan to the offer packet. HR (Neha) to sign-off on the $15k sign-on and confirm the 6-month review checkpoint wording.
- Timeline: Monica to present verbal offer to candidate by EOD Monday 16 Feb; formal offer to follow within 24–48 hours (DocuSign link included).

Monica — please confirm when the verbal is done and include the candidate's preferred start window. Neha — if you can confirm sign-on approval in the thread, I'll approve the offer language.

Thanks all,
Dylan
